messages.subject: Elevation clarification
parts:
Hi Mike!

Wanted to get some clarification on the capabilities of the elevation/aspect/slope portions of the micro functions (e.g. micro_era5). Does it extend to accounting for whether the sun is blocked by nearby mountains at certain times of day, or is it strictly limited to calculations based on the slope/aspect/elevation directly over the given point?

Best
Adam

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Elevation clarification
parts:
Hi Adam,
The horizon angles can be calculated from a DEM and passed to the microclimate model (argument 'hori') and this will capture effects of nearby mountains on direct beam solar (or you could use it to simulate the effects e.g. of a wall).
e.g.
      elev <- raster::extract(dem, c(lon, lat))[1]        
      xy <- data.frame(x = lon, y = lat)
      sp::coordinates(xy) = ~x + y
      sp::proj4string(xy) = "+init=epsg:4326"
      xy <- as.data.frame(sp::spTransform(xy, raster::crs(dem)))
      ha36 <- 0
      for (i in 0:35) {
        har <- horizonangle(dem, i * 10, raster::res(dem)[1])
        ha36[i + 1] <- atan(raster::extract(har, xy)) * (180/pi)
      }
      hori <- spline(x = ha36, n = 24, method =  'periodic')$y
      hori[hori < 0] <- 0
      hori[hori > 90] <- 90

All the best,
Mike
